resourceMaterial: Federal Government Financial Regulations (Revised to January 2009), Chapter 1, FR 102

The Public Procurement Act, 2007
The Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria
The Federal Inland Revenue Service (Establishment) Act

resourceMaterial: Federal Government Financial Regulations (Revised to January 2009), Chapter 1, FR 104

options: The Evidence Act, Cap E14 LFN 2004
The Finance (Control and Management) Act, Cap 144 LFN 1990
The Land Use Act, Cap L5 LFN 2004
The Pension Reform Act, 2004

source: Financial Regulations (Revised to January 2009), FR 104

resourceMaterial: Federal Government Financial Regulations (Revised to January 2009), Chapter 1, FR 105
question: Who issues the Financial Regulations from time to time, in accordance with existing laws and policies of government?
options: The Head of the Civil Service
The Auditor-General of the Federation
The Accountant-General of the Federation
The Minister of Finance

Chief Auditor responsible for the examination of receipts and payments of the government
Principal Adviser to the Minister of Finance on the preparation of the annual estimates
Chief Accounting Officer for the vote books and expenditure of every ministry

options: The Head of the Civil Service
The Accountant-General of the Federation
The Permanent Secretary of each ministry
The Auditor-General of the Federation

source: Financial Regulations (Revised to January 2009), FR 107(n)

Value-for-Money Audit
Appropriation Audit

Appropriation (Expenditure) Audit
Value-for-Money (Performance) Audit
Systems and Procedures Audit

source: Financial Regulations (Revised to January 2009), FR 109(i)(d)

resourceMaterial: Federal Government Financial Regulations (Revised to January 2009), Chapter 1, FR 110
question: Who shall, at all reasonable times, have free access to the books of account, files, safes and security documents of federal ministries and extra-ministerial offices?
options: The Accountant-General and the Auditor-General or their representatives
The Accountant-General and the Head of Service or their representatives
The Auditor-General and the Minister of Finance or their representatives
The Accountant-General and the Accounting Officer of the ministry concerned

resourceMaterial: Federal Government Financial Regulations (Revised to January 2009), Chapter 1, FR 112(e)
question: Ensuring personal appearance before the Public Accounts Committee to answer audit queries is a function of the:
options: Sub-Accounting Officer
Accounting Officer
Auditor-General
Revenue Collector

source: Financial Regulations (Revised to January 2009), FR 112(e)

resourceMaterial: Federal Government Financial Regulations (Revised to January 2009), Chapter 1, FR 112(l)
question: Under FR 112, revenue collected by a ministry must be:
options: Retained in the ministry's strong room until the end of the quarter and then lodged
Applied first to settle outstanding imprest, with the balance remitted
Paid into the ministry's bank account and used to fund urgent recurrent items
Remitted promptly to the appropriate authorities and not spent

source: Financial Regulations (Revised to January 2009), FR 112(l)

resourceMaterial: Federal Government Financial Regulations (Revised to January 2009), Chapter 1, FR 116
question: Who is the political head of a parastatal or extra-ministerial office?
options: The Permanent Secretary or Chief Executive of the parastatal or extra-ministerial office
The Minister of the supervising ministry, acting through the Accounting Officer
The Chairman of the parastatal or extra-ministerial office (or as defined in the extant laws governing it)
The Head of Service, acting on the advice of the Accountant-General

source: Financial Regulations (Revised to January 2009), FR 116

resourceMaterial: Federal Government Financial Regulations (Revised to January 2009), Chapter 1, FR 117(ii)
question: A directive from a Political Head results in unauthorised expenditure. In the case of a ministry, the Accounting Officer escapes responsibility only if he has reported the matter to:
options: The Head of Service
The Auditor-General
The Minister of Finance
The Accountant-General
explanation: FR 117(ii): the report goes to the Head of Service for ministries and extra-ministerial offices, and to the Minister for parastatals.
source: Financial Regulations (Revised to January 2009), FR 117(ii)

resourceMaterial: Federal Government Financial Regulations (Revised to January 2009), Chapter 1, FR 118(ii)(a)
question: Which of the following is a responsibility of the Political Head under FR 118?
options: Rendering monthly transcripts of the ministry's accounts to the Accountant-General
Maintaining the main and subsidiary ledgers of the ministry's expenditure
Preparing the monthly bank reconciliation statements for the Auditor-General
Endorsing the annual budget proposals of the ministry to the Budget Office

source: Financial Regulations (Revised to January 2009), FR 118(ii)(a)

resourceMaterial: Federal Government Financial Regulations (Revised to January 2009), Chapter 1, FR 120

options: Imprest-holder
Accounting Officer
Officer Controlling Expenditure
Revenue Collector

resourceMaterial: Federal Government Financial Regulations (Revised to January 2009), Chapter 1, FR 121

Control of a sub-head, or a specified amount of a sub-head, has been delegated by the appropriate Accounting Officer
A general warrant has been issued for all payments under a head of the Estimates
The Minister of Finance has delegated control of the ministry's whole Capital Estimates
explanation: FR 121 defines the Officer Controlling Expenditure.
source: Financial Regulations (Revised to January 2009), FR 121

resourceMaterial: Federal Government Financial Regulations (Revised to January 2009), Chapter 1, FR 122

options: Head of Service
Auditor-General
Accountant-General
Minister of Finance
source: Financial Regulations (Revised to January 2009), FR 122

resourceMaterial: Federal Government Financial Regulations (Revised to January 2009), Chapter 1, FR 123(i)(p)
question: Within how many days must an officer with financial responsibilities reply to formal queries from the Accountant-General and the Auditor-General?
options: Twenty-one days
Fourteen days
Thirty days
Forty-five days
explanation: FR 123(i)(p) requires a reply within twenty-one days giving the full particulars requested.
source: Financial Regulations (Revised to January 2009), FR 123(i)(p)

resourceMaterial: Federal Government Financial Regulations (Revised to January 2009), Chapter 1, FR 123(i)(j)
question: An officer discovers a minor cash deficiency that was not caused by theft or fraud. Under FR 123, he must:
options: Report it to the Auditor-General and await instructions before making it good
Charge it to a suspense account until the next annual audit is completed
Promptly make good the deficiency and report details in writing to the appropriate officer
Recover it through monthly salary deductions approved by the Head of Service

source: Financial Regulations (Revised to January 2009), FR 123(i)(j)

resourceMaterial: Federal Government Financial Regulations (Revised to January 2009), Chapter 1, FR 124
question: The Auditor-General's responsibility for checking and reporting shortcomings in public accounts:
options: Shifts pecuniary liability for any irregularity to the Auditor-General's department once reported
Applies only to the accounts maintained in the Accountant-General's office
Relieves accounting officers of liability once an audit report has been issued without query
Does not absolve any accounting officer from his own responsibility for complying with the regulations
explanation: FR 124: officers remain personally and pecuniarily responsible.
source: Financial Regulations (Revised to January 2009), FR 124

resourceMaterial: Federal Government Financial Regulations (Revised to January 2009), Chapter 1, FR 126
question: Who shall from time to time cause surprise inspections to be carried out on the accounts of the officers referred to in FR 123?
options: The Head of Service
The Accountant-General
The Tenders Board
The Political Head of the ministry
explanation: FR 126. Accounting Officers likewise make surprise checks on the accounts of their subordinates.
source: Financial Regulations (Revised to January 2009), FR 126

resourceMaterial: Federal Government Financial Regulations (Revised to January 2009), Chapter 1, FR 127
question: Where a matter affecting a ministry's accounts is not provided for in the Regulations, the Accounting Officer shall:
options: Refer to the Office of the Auditor-General for a ruling
Refer to the Office of the Accountant-General for advice
Refer to the Head of the Civil Service for a ruling
Refer to the Minister of Finance for a special warrant
explanation: FR 127: any departure from the Regulations is permitted only with the concurrence of the Accountant-General.
source: Financial Regulations (Revised to January 2009), FR 127

resourceMaterial: Federal Government Financial Regulations (Revised to January 2009), Chapter 3, FR 301
question: Under FR 301, no expenditure may be incurred on any service, whether or not it is included in the Estimates, unless authorised by:
options: A warrant issued by the Accountant-General of the Federation
An authority issued by the Head of the Civil Service
A warrant issued by the Minister of Finance
A circular issued by the Budget Office

source: Financial Regulations (Revised to January 2009), FR 301

resourceMaterial: Federal Government Financial Regulations (Revised to January 2009), Chapter 3, FR 301
question: An officer controlling a vote incurs expenditure without the proper authority. Under FR 301 he does so:
options: With the shared liability of the Accountant-General and the Auditor-General
With the approval implied by the passage of the Appropriation Act
On the joint responsibility of his Accounting Officer and the Political Head
On his sole responsibility and is held pecuniarily responsible for his actions

options: Development Fund (Special) Warrant
Supplementary (Statutory Expenditure) Warrant
Provisional General Warrant
Virement Warrant

resourceMaterial: Federal Government Financial Regulations (Revised to January 2009), Chapter 3, FR 307
question: Expenditure incurred under the Supplementary (Contingencies) Warrant procedure is subject to:
options: Automatic lapse at the end of the quarter unless the Auditor-General certifies it
Direct charge to the Contingencies Fund without further approval of the National Assembly
Retrospective approval by the Federal Executive Council through a general warrant
The covering approval of the National Assembly at its next meeting, through a Supplementary Appropriation Act

resourceMaterial: Federal Government Financial Regulations (Revised to January 2009), Chapter 3, FR 308

options: Provisional General Warrant
Supplementary General Warrant
Virement Warrant
Development Fund General Warrant
source: Financial Regulations (Revised to January 2009), FR 308

options: Create a new sub-head or re-introduce items disallowed by the Estimates Committee or the National Assembly
Meet unforeseen additional provision under a sub-head
Move savings between sub-heads of the same Head
Cover shortfalls in overhead costs within the approved limit
source: Financial Regulations (Revised to January 2009), FR 310(b)

resourceMaterial: Federal Government Financial Regulations (Revised to January 2009), Chapter 3, FR 310(c)
question: Virement shall not apply to:
options: Additional provision required to meet unforeseen circumstances arising under the same Head
Variations in expenditure approved by the National Assembly during the year
Queries raised by the Auditor-General in respect of improper expenditure already incurred
Savings available on other sub-heads within the same Head of Expenditure

resourceMaterial: Federal Government Financial Regulations (Revised to January 2009), Chapter 3, FR 311
question: Any variation in the establishment or rates of allowances authorised in the Estimates must receive the approval of the Minister of Finance and:
options: The Office of the Accountant-General, with the approval notified to the Head of Service
The Federal Executive Council, with the approval notified to the National Assembly
The Office of the Head of Civil Service, with the approval notified to the Auditor-General
The Budget Office, with the approval notified to the Accountant-General
source: Financial Regulations (Revised to January 2009), FR 311

resourceMaterial: Federal Government Financial Regulations (Revised to January 2009), Chapter 3, FR 312
question: A Supplementary (Statutory) Expenditure Warrant is issued for additional expenditure in respect of votes that are:
options: Payable only from the Contingencies Fund after the close of the financial year
Chargeable against the Consolidated Revenue Fund by virtue of the Constitution
Charged to the Development Fund by resolution of the National Assembly
Funded from internally generated revenue approved by the Minister of Finance
source: Financial Regulations (Revised to January 2009), FR 312

resourceMaterial: Federal Government Financial Regulations (Revised to January 2009), Chapter 3, FR 313

The approval of the Federal Executive Council, sought by application for a special warrant
The consent of the Accountant-General, sought by application for a general warrant
The concurrence of the Auditor-General, sought by application for a supplementary warrant

Treasury Form 146
Treasury Form 15
General Form 57

options: Allowed in the first quarter only
Not allowed, and vice versa
Allowed up to ten per cent of the sub-head
Allowed with the Accountant-General's consent

source: Financial Regulations (Revised to January 2009), FR 316(iii)

resourceMaterial: Federal Government Financial Regulations (Revised to January 2009), Chapter 3, FR 316(v)
question: A register is kept for all approved virements. Within what period must details be forwarded to the Accountant-General and the Auditor-General?
options: Seven days
Six months
One month
Three months
source: Financial Regulations (Revised to January 2009), FR 316(v)

resourceMaterial: Federal Government Financial Regulations (Revised to January 2009), Chapter 3, FR 317
question: On receipt of a virement warrant, expenditure against the sub-head from which the provision was transferred must not exceed:
options: The amount of the previous year's expenditure
The original approved provision
The balance of the receiving sub-head
The reduced balance remaining in that sub-head

Report of the Auditor-General
Direction of the Head of Service
Circular of the Accountant-General

options: Revenue Mobilisation column of the Estimates
"Balance to Complete" column of the Estimates
Statutory Expenditure column of the Estimates
Contingencies column of the Estimates

options: The National Assembly acting through its Appropriation Committee
The Minister of Finance acting alone
The Head of the Civil Service of the Federation
The Federal Executive Council

options: Within the same Head of Expenditure in the Capital Estimates, and not for a new project
Between different Heads of Expenditure in the Capital Estimates, provided the project is approved
Within the same Head of Expenditure in the Recurrent Estimates, including personnel costs
Across any Heads of the Capital Estimates, but only for projects already in the Estimates

options: The Auditor-General
The Accountant-General
The National Planning Commission
The Head of Civil Service of the Federation
source: Financial Regulations (Revised to January 2009), FR 325

resourceMaterial: Federal Government Financial Regulations (Revised to January 2009), Chapter 3, FR 326
question: The authority to incur expenditure from any of the other Public Funds of the Government is:
options: The appropriate warrant signed by the Accountant-General and addressed to the Auditor-General
A general warrant signed by the Head of Service and addressed to the Accounting Officer
A Treasury circular signed by the Permanent Secretary and addressed to the Budget Office
The appropriate warrant signed by the Minister of Finance and addressed to the Accountant-General

In the Appropriation Warrant only
In the Auditor-General's annual report
In the Treasury Circulars

question: The ultimate responsibility to the Federal Executive Council for the control of votes rests at all times with the:
options: Revenue Collectors
Accounting Officers
Auditor-General
Sub-Accounting Officers

resourceMaterial: Federal Government Financial Regulations (Revised to January 2009), Chapter 4, FR 404
question: An officer to whom day-to-day control of expenditure has been delegated may NOT sub-delegate that responsibility:
options: Without the approval of the Auditor-General
Under any circumstances
Without the knowledge and approval of the officer controlling the vote
Without a resolution of the Public Accounts Committee

Keep a vote book and send annual returns of expenditure, supported by receipts, to the Auditor-General
Keep a vote book and send monthly returns of expenditure, liabilities and balance, supported by copies of paid vouchers, to the issuing ministry
Keep a ledger and send weekly returns of liabilities, supported by copies of LPOs, to the issuing ministry

options: The Auditor-General
The Head of Service
The Minister of Finance
The Accountant-General

source: Financial Regulations (Revised to January 2009), FR 408

resourceMaterial: Federal Government Financial Regulations (Revised to January 2009), Chapter 4, FR 409
question: Where fraud is suspected in a voucher, the officer controlling the vote shall immediately investigate, report the circumstances and:
options: Inform the police
Reclassify the voucher to another sub-head
Close the vote book for the year
Wait for the next audit

source: Financial Regulations (Revised to January 2009), FR 409

resourceMaterial: Federal Government Financial Regulations (Revised to January 2009), Chapter 4, FR 409
question: An unauthorised payment is made because of an incorrect certificate or entry on a voucher. Who is held responsible and surcharged?
options: The Accountant-General or the Head of Finance and Accounts
The certifying officer or the Sub-Accounting Officer
The Auditor-General or the Chief Internal Auditor
The Political Head or the Permanent Secretary of the ministry

resourceMaterial: Federal Government Financial Regulations (Revised to January 2009), Chapter 4, FR 410

Only that the amount claimed is within the approved provision for the financial year
That the voucher has been entered in the cash book and the payee has signed a receipt
The accuracy of every detail on the voucher, including that the services were performed and prices are fair

The full contract sum is paid, and the penalty is recovered later from the contractor's next claim
Only the net sum is paid, and the deduction is credited to the Contingencies Fund
The net sum is paid, and the deduction is credited to the Development Fund

Drawn to set in reserve to meet impending payments, or carried to a deposit or suspense account
Entered in the vote book
Left to lapse at the end of the financial year

The Head of Service
The Accountant-General
The contractor concerned

resourceMaterial: Federal Government Financial Regulations (Revised to January 2009), Chapter 4, FR 417
question: Expenditure incorrectly charged to a vote shall be:

Written off immediately
Disallowed
Ratified by the Accounting Officer

The expenditure sub-head of the paying ministry, with a note of recovery
The Deposit Account of the Accountant-General, until the paying ministry is reimbursed
The Contingencies Fund account, pending regularisation by a Supplementary Warrant

The officers controlling votes
The Permanent Secretary as Accounting Officer
The Political Head of the ministry

The Accounting Officer, who will report the alteration to the Auditor-General

The Permanent Secretary's office, from the ministry's vote for personnel costs
The Government, except for treatment obtained outside the officer's station

In special circumstances where government facilities are unavailable, or an emergency referral is certified by a Medical Board
Where the officer's private doctor certifies that the treatment was necessary

Written recommendation by any government doctor and approval of the Permanent Secretary
A request by the officer supported by a foreign hospital's invitation letter
Official recommendation by the Civil Service Commission and approval of the Accountant-General

Statutory declarations by the officer, witnessed by a colleague on the same grade level

Referral to a Medical Board for consideration of invaliding from the service if incapable of further efficient service

Payment in accordance with the rates set by the hospital management board

Immediately report the injury to the Department and submit the required accident/injury report forms for medical evaluation
Report the injury at the end of the month through the Accounts Department

Recommend the amount of compensation to be paid to the officer by the Department
Forward the particulars of the injuries to the Police for investigation of possible negligence

explanation: Rule 080107: Governed by official leave/time-out provisions or approved clinic visits under medical procedures.
source: Lagos State Public Service Rules, Rule 080107

question: What record-keeping duty does a Department maintain regarding sick staff?
options: Keeping only the officer's name and grade level and reporting sickness at year end
Recording sick leave days and deducting them automatically from annual leave
Recording addresses, making enquiries about absentees, and reporting staff sickness to ensure welfare and control
Maintaining a register of medical certificates and forwarding it to the Civil Service Commission
explanation: Rule 080307: Departments maintain records of addresses, make enquiries about absentees, and report sickness for welfare and control.
source: Lagos State Public Service Rules, Rule 080307

question: Who bears responsibility for inquiries about staff reported absent due to alleged sickness?
options: The Medical Officer of the nearest government hospital through the Medical Board
The officer's immediate superior through the Civil Service Commission
The Director of Personnel Management through the Head of Service
The Permanent Secretary/Head of Department through personnel management channels
explanation: Rule 080307: The Permanent Secretary/Head of Department through personnel management channels bears responsibility.
source: Lagos State Public Service Rules, Rule 080307

question: Are officers embarked as invalids entitled to special passage assistance?
options: No, such officers must pay their own passage and claim a refund after recovery
Yes, repatriation passages and medical travel facilitation according to service regulations
Yes, but only first-class passage to be paid for by the officer's family
No, such officers are entitled only to the medical costs and not to passages
explanation: Rule 080204: Officers embarked as invalids are entitled to repatriation passages and medical travel facilitation.
source: Lagos State Public Service Rules, Rule 080204

question: A clerk asks to see a colleague's medical file out of curiosity. What is the correct position?
options: He can, because medical files are open to all staff in the same ministry
He can, if he obtains the permission of the Permanent Secretary alone
He cannot, because medical documents relating to officers are confidential
He can, provided the colleague has no objection and the Registry keeps a record
explanation: Rule 080102: Medical documents relating to officers are strictly confidential and cannot be inspected out of curiosity.
source: Lagos State Public Service Rules, Rule 080102

question: A new appointee brings a fitness certificate from a private clinic. Is this sufficient for first appointment?
options: No, he must be certified medically fit by a State Government Medical Officer
Yes, a certificate from any registered private clinic is sufficient
Yes, provided the private clinic's certificate is stamped by the Permanent Secretary
No, he must be certified fit by a Federal Government Medical Officer
explanation: Rule 080103: A new appointee must be certified medically fit by a State Government Medical Officer.
source: Lagos State Public Service Rules, Rule 080103

question: Which statement about medical examination on first appointment is correct?
options: It is optional and required only for officers on Grade Level 07 and above
It is mandatory for every candidate on initial entry into government service
It is mandatory only for candidates who have previously been ill
It is required only at the time of confirmation of appointment
explanation: Rule 080103: Medical examination is mandatory for every candidate on initial entry into government service.
source: Lagos State Public Service Rules, Rule 080103

question: Which of the following is NOT recognized as cover for absence from duty due to illness?
options: A certificate from a registered government medical officer
A certificate from a recognized approved medical practitioner
An official Medical Certificate
A note written by the officer himself
explanation: Rules 080301 & 080302: A note written by the officer himself is not recognized as medical cover for absence.
source: Lagos State Public Service Rules, Rules 080301 and 080302

question: Are casual, sick and maternity leave inclusive of Saturdays, Sundays and public holidays?
options: Yes, they are inclusive of Saturdays, Sundays and public holidays
No, they are counted on working days only, like annual leave
No, they exclude public holidays but include Saturdays and Sundays
No, they exclude Saturdays and Sundays but include public holidays
explanation: Rule 120207: Casual, sick and maternity leave are inclusive of Saturdays, Sundays and public holidays.
source: Lagos State Public Service Rules, Rule 120207

question: An officer stays away for three days without any medical authority. How is the absence treated?
options: As casual leave of three days, with no further consequences
As sick leave, provided the officer produces a medical certificate afterwards
As absence without leave, making him liable to disciplinary action
As a minor irregularity, for which a verbal warning is enough
explanation: Rule 080312: Uncovered absence is treated as absence without leave liable to disciplinary action.
source: Lagos State Public Service Rules, Rule 080312

question: Which body must recommend medical treatment overseas for a public servant?
options: The officer's family
A private hospital abroad
The Ministry's Accounts Department
A duly constituted Medical Board
explanation: Rule 080207: Overseas medical treatment must be recommended by a duly constituted Medical Board.
source: Lagos State Public Service Rules, Rule 080207

question: An officer needs emergency medical care while on official duty overseas. Who generally bears the cost?
options: The officer, since all overseas medical expenses are personal
The Government, as official duty overseas attracts government medical coverage
The host country's government, under reciprocal arrangements with Nigeria
The officer's private insurer, with the Government refunding only after the tour
explanation: Rules 080206 & 080207: The Government bears medical costs for officers on official overseas duty.
source: Lagos State Public Service Rules, Rules 080206 and 080207

question: An officer directed to appear before a Medical Board says he is too busy. Is this acceptable?
options: Yes, provided he informs the Permanent Secretary of his reasons in writing
Yes, the board may be rescheduled once at the officer's convenience
No, he has a strict duty to appear and comply with the board's recommendations
No, but he may appear through a representative with a written authority
explanation: Rule 080306: Officers have an imperative duty to appear and comply with the Medical Board's recommendations.
source: Lagos State Public Service Rules, Rule 080306

question: Who verifies a report sent by a private practitioner in place of attendance at government clinics?
options: Government medical authorities
The Permanent Secretary of the officer's ministry
The Director of Personnel Management
The Head of Service
explanation: Rule 080310: Government medical authorities must verify reports from private practitioners.
source: Lagos State Public Service Rules, Rule 080310

question: Which information must a sick officer at home give his employer?
options: His next of kin's address, so that the family can be informed
His address, so that he can be contacted
The name of his private doctor, so that records can be verified
The expected date of resumption, so that his duties can be reassigned
explanation: Rules 080303-080305: A sick officer at home must notify his address so he can be contacted.
source: Lagos State Public Service Rules, Rules 080303 to 080305

question: How often is the medical check-up for public servants instituted under government health procedures?
options: Every ten years
Only on retirement
Only on first appointment
Annually
explanation: Rule 080210: The public service medical check-up is instituted annually.
source: Lagos State Public Service Rules, Rule 080210

question: To whom should an officer injured in the course of official duty first report the injury?
options: His Department, immediately
The nearest Police Station, within 24 hours
The Medical Board, within seven days
The Head of Service, at the end of treatment
explanation: Rule 080402: The injury must be reported immediately to his Department.
source: Lagos State Public Service Rules, Rule 080402

question: For what purpose does a Medical Officer issue a report on injuries sustained in the line of duty?
options: Deciding the officer's promotion
Deciding the officer's transfer
Compensation processing
Computing the officer's leave allowance
explanation: Rule 080403: Reports on line-of-duty injuries are issued for compensation processing.
source: Lagos State Public Service Rules, Rule 080403

question: Which of the following is covered by government repatriation provisions in Chapter 8?
options: Death of an officer's parent while the officer is on annual leave abroad
Death of a retired officer overseas while visiting relatives
Death of an officer's child at a foreign school during a vacation
Death of a Nigerian officer or his spouse overseas while on official duty
explanation: Rule 080501: Government repatriation covers death of a Nigerian officer or spouse overseas while on official duty.
source: Lagos State Public Service Rules, Rule 080501

question: Which of the following is a valid ground for refunding medical expenses incurred outside government facilities?
options: A private consultation chosen by the officer for convenience
An emergency referral certified by a Medical Board
Treatment obtained at a private hospital before reporting the illness
Treatment received while the officer was on annual leave abroad
explanation: Rule 080203: An emergency referral certified by a Medical Board is a valid ground for refund.
source: Lagos State Public Service Rules, Rule 080203

question: Under what circumstance is an officer considered for invaliding?
options: When he has been absent on sick leave for any single period of more than one month
When he has taken casual leave on more than three occasions in a leave year
When aggregate sick leave limits are reached and he is incapable of further efficient service
When his Permanent Secretary considers his performance below the expected standard
explanation: Rule 080315: When aggregate sick leave limits are reached and the officer is incapable of further efficient service.
source: Lagos State Public Service Rules, Rule 080315

question: What is 'Sick Leave'?
options: Authorized leave granted on certified medical grounds supported by approved medical certificates or medical boards
Leave granted on the officer's own request to attend to family health matters, without certification
Leave granted automatically to every officer for a number of days each year for rest
Leave granted by a Permanent Secretary on personal assessment of the officer's condition
explanation: Rule 120233: Sick leave is authorized leave granted on certified medical grounds.
source: Lagos State Public Service Rules, Rule 120233

question: An officer on annual vacation falls ill and has a proper sick leave certificate. What may happen to the annual leave?
options: It is forfeited for the days of illness, and the officer must resume duty immediately after recovery
It may be credited/suspended and converted to sick leave as appropriate
It is cancelled outright and the officer must apply for new annual leave in the next year
It continues in full, and the sick days are treated as additional annual leave
explanation: Chapters 8 & 12: Annual leave may be suspended/credited and converted to sick leave upon proper medical certification.
source: Lagos State Public Service Rules, Chapters 8 and 12

question: After obtaining a certificate from an outside doctor, when should the officer report to his department?
options: Within 48 hours of issuance
Within seven days of issuance
At the end of the period covered by the certificate
Without delay, within 24 hours of issuance
explanation: Rules 080304 & 080310: Report without delay, within 24 hours of issuance.
source: Lagos State Public Service Rules, Rules 080304 and 080310

question: How is 'Whistle blowing / Grievance' broadly defined in the context of service petitions?
options: Formal reporting or lodging of legitimate grievances regarding administrative injustice, unfair treatment or service malpractices through prescribed channels
Informal discussion of personal disagreements among colleagues in a ministry without any record
Public disclosure of administrative matters through the press when departmental channels are slow
Reporting of criminal offences by officers directly to the Police and the courts
explanation: Rule 100101: Defined as formal reporting of legitimate grievances regarding administrative injustice or malpractices.
source: Lagos State Public Service Rules, Rule 100101

question: What is strictly prohibited regarding external influence in petitions?
options: Copying the petition to the officer's trade union for follow-up with the Permanent Secretary
Seeking external political, ethnic or prominent influence to lobby or press petitions instead of using internal service procedures
Writing to the Head of Service to request a hearing before the petition is routed
Asking a senior colleague in the same ministry to review the petition before submission
explanation: Rule 100203: Seeking external political, ethnic or prominent influence to lobby or press petitions is strictly prohibited.
source: Lagos State Public Service Rules, Rule 100203

question: What requirement governs the identity of a petitioner?
options: A petitioner may withhold his name if he fears victimisation, and the petition is still treated as valid
Only the petitioner's initials and service number need be disclosed on the petition
The identity of the petitioner must be clearly disclosed; anonymous petitions are generally disregarded
The petitioner's identity is disclosed only to the Permanent Secretary and not to the appellate authority
explanation: Rule 100204: The identity of the petitioner must be clearly disclosed; anonymous petitions are generally disregarded.
source: Lagos State Public Service Rules, Rule 100204

question: How must a petition submitted on behalf of an illiterate person be handled?
options: Properly endorsed and accompanied by a jurat indicating the writer/interpreter, in accordance with Illiterates Protection laws
Signed by the illiterate person alone, with a thumbprint witnessed by a colleague on the same grade
Endorsed by the illiterate person's Permanent Secretary and accompanied by a medical report
Written by a legal practitioner and submitted directly to the Civil Service Commission
explanation: Rule 100205: Must be accompanied by a jurat indicating the writer/interpreter under Illiterates Protection laws.
source: Lagos State Public Service Rules, Rule 100205

question: What is the proper routing of a formal official petition?
options: Sent directly to the final appellate authority, with copies to the Permanent Secretary
Routed sequentially through immediate superior officers and the Permanent Secretary to the final appellate authority
Routed through the Director of Personnel Management and the Head of Service in turn
Routed through the officer's trade union and the Permanent Secretary to the Governor
explanation: Rule 100206: Routed sequentially through immediate superior officers and the Permanent Secretary to final appellate authority.
source: Lagos State Public Service Rules, Rule 100206

question: What can cause a petition to be disqualified or rejected?
options: Lack of a covering letter, failure to attach a medical report, or use of a typed signature
Submission through the immediate superior officer with the Permanent Secretary's endorsement
Excessive length, failure to cite legal authorities, or submission through a legal practitioner
Lack of proper identity, failure to exhaust internal channels, use of foul language, or external political lobbying
explanation: Rule 100208: Disqualification occurs for lack of proper identity, failure to exhaust internal channels, foul language, or political lobbying.
source: Lagos State Public Service Rules, Rule 100208

question: Why must any delay in submitting a petition be explained by the petitioner?
options: To establish promptness and ensure the matter is not stale or statute-barred under administrative limitation rules
To enable the Permanent Secretary to compute interest on any amounts claimed by the petitioner
To establish that the petitioner has the support of colleagues who share the grievance
To ensure the petition is registered by the Registry before the end of the financial year
explanation: Rule 100208: To establish promptness and ensure the matter is not stale or statute-barred under administrative limitation rules.
source: Lagos State Public Service Rules, Rule 100208

question: Can an officer appeal against a disciplinary penalty imposed by a Personnel Management Board?
options: No, a decision of a Personnel Management Board is final and not subject to any appeal
Yes, but only to the Permanent Secretary of the officer's ministry
Yes, but only to the Head of Service, whose decision is final
Yes, through formal appeal channels to the Civil Service Commission or the appropriate appellate body
explanation: Chapter 10 & 18: Appeals lie through formal appeal channels to the Civil Service Commission or appropriate appellate body.
source: Lagos State Public Service Rules, Chapter 10 and Chapter 18, Section 6

question: Who handles appeals relating to senior officers on Grade Level 07 and above?
options: The Head of Service or the Permanent Secretary of the officer's ministry
The Personnel Management Board of the officer's ministry
The State Civil Service Commission or the relevant Extra-Ministerial Body
The Office of Establishments and Training, through the Director of Personnel Management
explanation: Chapter 10 & 2: The State Civil Service Commission or relevant Extra-Ministerial Body handles appeals for GL 07 and above.
source: Lagos State Public Service Rules, Chapter 10 and Chapter 2, Section 6

question: Is an officer permitted to attach classified official documents as exhibits in a petition?
options: No, unauthorized disclosure or abstraction of classified documents violates the Official Secrets Act and is serious misconduct
Yes, if the exhibits are certified as true copies by the Permanent Secretary
Yes, provided the officer marks the documents as confidential for the appellate authority
Yes, but only if the documents were obtained from the officer's own department
explanation: Rule 040517 & Ch 10: Unauthorized disclosure of classified documents violates the Official Secrets Act and is serious misconduct.
source: Lagos State Public Service Rules, Rule 040517 and Chapter 10

question: Within what period should petitions against promotion results typically be lodged?
options: Within 3 months of the announcement
Within 12 months of the announcement
Within 30 days of the announcement
Within 6 months of the announcement
explanation: Rule 020602(iv): Petitions against promotion results should be lodged within 6 months of announcement.
source: Lagos State Public Service Rules, Rule 020602(iv)

question: What is the administrative duty of a Permanent Secretary upon receiving a petition routed through him against an administrative decision?
options: Forward it with pertinent comments, factual records and file notes to the appropriate appellate commission without undue delay
Hold it until the Permanent Secretary has investigated and decided the matter personally
Return it to the petitioner with advice to withdraw it before routing it further
Forward it directly to the Governor without comments and keep copies in the registry
explanation: Chapter 10: The Permanent Secretary must forward the petition with pertinent comments, factual records and file notes without undue delay.
source: Lagos State Public Service Rules, Chapter 10, Sections 1 and 2

question: Does lodging a petition automatically suspend the execution of a lawful disciplinary penalty?
options: Yes, the penalty is suspended automatically until the appeal is determined
Yes, but only for the first thirty days after the petition is lodged
No, the penalty remains in force unless specifically stayed or set aside by the competent appellate authority
No, but the officer is paid full salary until the appeal is determined
explanation: Chapter 10: A disciplinary penalty remains in force unless specifically stayed or set aside by the competent appellate authority.
source: Lagos State Public Service Rules, Chapter 10, General Principles

question: What support do public service rules provide for settling internal workplace grievances informally?
options: Informal arbitration by the officer's trade union with a binding effect on the ministry
Referral of the grievance to the Police and the courts for informal resolution
Automatic transfer of the aggrieved officer to another ministry to reduce friction
Counselling, mentoring, coaching and administrative dialogue through supervisors before escalating to formal petitions
explanation: Rule 040302 & Ch 10: Counselling, mentoring, coaching and administrative dialogue through supervisors before escalating.
source: Lagos State Public Service Rules, Rule 040302 and Chapter 10

question: Are officers permitted to engage external media or newspapers to air service grievances?
options: Yes, provided the officer does not mention names or the ministry concerned
No, public utterances, press interviews or publishing grievances without express government permission violate conduct rules
Yes, but only after a formal petition has been unanswered for six months
Yes, if the Permanent Secretary is informed in writing within seven days
explanation: Rule 040522: Public utterances or publishing grievances in external media without express permission violate conduct rules.
source: Lagos State Public Service Rules, Rule 040522

question: Can an officer be victimized for submitting a legitimate, properly channeled petition?
options: Yes, if the petition is later found to be without merit after investigation
Yes, the ministry may re-post the officer pending the outcome of the petition
No, victimization for exercising legitimate petition rights is prohibited and constitutes administrative misconduct
Yes, but only where the petition criticised a superior officer
explanation: Chapter 10: Victimization for submitting a legitimate, properly channeled petition is strictly prohibited and constitutes misconduct.
source: Lagos State Public Service Rules, Chapter 10, General Principles

question: What is required when a petition contains multiple complex allegations involving financial records?
options: Detailed auditing reports, vouchers and documentary evidence must be attached to substantiate the claims
A sworn affidavit of the petitioner supported by a statement from a legal practitioner
Statements from colleagues who witnessed the transactions in question
A written undertaking by the petitioner to bear the costs of any investigation
explanation: Rule 100202: Detailed auditing reports, vouchers and documentary evidence must be attached to substantiate allegations.
source: Lagos State Public Service Rules, Rule 100202

question: How are appeals from parastatal organizations handled regarding petition routes?
options: Routed through the Governing Board and the Civil Service Commission to the Head of Service
Routed through the Parastatal Governing Board/Council and supervisory Ministry to the Head of Government or Civil Service Commission as applicable
Sent directly to the Head of Government without any intermediate authority
Routed through the parastatal's Chief Executive to the Auditor-General for the State
explanation: Rule 180601: Routed through Parastatal Governing Board/Council and supervisory Ministry to the Head of Government or Commission.
source: Lagos State Public Service Rules, Rule 180601

question: What duty does an officer have regarding truthfulness in petitions?
options: He must state facts truthfully, but false petitions attract only a verbal warning
He is free to state his belief of the facts, and false statements made in good faith are protected
He must state facts truthfully; malicious and false petitions constitute minor misconduct punishable by a query
He must state facts truthfully; malicious and false petitions constitute serious misconduct punishable by dismissal
explanation: Rule 040502 & Ch 10: Facts must be stated truthfully; malicious and false petitions constitute serious misconduct punishable by dismissal.
source: Lagos State Public Service Rules, Rule 040502(xxvii) and Chapter 10

question: What is the role of the Public Service Office in petitions and appeals?
options: To coordinate administrative reviews, policy interpretations and advisory processing on personnel appeals
To adjudicate on personnel appeals and give binding decisions for the Civil Service Commission
To investigate criminal allegations in petitions and prosecute offenders before the courts
To receive and register petitions on behalf of the Permanent Secretaries of all ministries
explanation: Chapters 6 & 10: The Public Service Office coordinates administrative reviews, policy interpretations and advisory processing.
source: Lagos State Public Service Rules, Chapters 6 and 10

question: How many copies of a petition are normally required for administrative processing?
options: A single original copy, which is photocopied by the Registry for onward transmission
Exactly five copies, one for each authority in the routing chain
Multiple prescribed copies, as specified in administrative guidelines (usually duplicate or triplicate)
As many copies as the petitioner chooses, as the Rules prescribe no number
explanation: Rule 100207: Multiple prescribed copies, as specified in guidelines (usually duplicate or triplicate).
source: Lagos State Public Service Rules, Rule 100207

question: What is the timeframe limit for forwarding disciplinary appeal files by ministries to central commissions?
options: Within 3 to 7 days of receipt
Within 45 to 60 days of receipt
Within 90 to 120 days of receipt
Within 14 to 30 days of receipt
explanation: Chapter 10: Disciplinary appeal files should be forwarded to central commissions within 14 to 30 days of receipt.
source: Lagos State Public Service Rules, Chapter 10, Sections 1 and 2

question: What happens if a petitioner dies while an appeal is pending?
options: The petition abates automatically and no benefit or adjustment may be pursued by the estate
Terminal benefits or estate representatives may pursue outstanding financial entitlements or adjustments in accordance with estate laws
The petition is transferred to the Governor for a final decision regardless of the estate
The Permanent Secretary decides on all outstanding entitlements without reference to estate laws
explanation: Rule 020705(a) & Ch 10: Terminal benefits or estate representatives may pursue outstanding financial entitlements.
source: Lagos State Public Service Rules, Rule 020705(a) and Chapter 10

question: Are legal practitioners permitted to represent officers during internal administrative panel hearings of petitions?
options: Legal practitioners are always entitled to represent officers at every internal panel hearing
Legal practitioners are never permitted to attend internal panels in any capacity
It is governed by administrative panel rules; inquiries are primarily internal, and legal counsel depends on the gravity and terms of reference authorized by the Commission
Legal practitioners may represent officers only where the Permanent Secretary invites them in writing
explanation: Chapters 4 & 10: Inquiries are primarily internal; legal representation depends on panel rules and Commission authorization.
source: Lagos State Public Service Rules, Chapters 4 and 10

question: Where do final appeals lie for matters within the constitutional jurisdiction of the Lagos State Civil Service Commission?
options: To the State Civil Service Commission / competent Courts of Law as provided by the Constitution and Laws of Lagos State
To the Head of Service, whose decision is final and cannot be questioned in any court
To the Permanent Secretary of the officer's ministry, whose decision is final
To the Executive Council of the State, with no recourse to the Courts of Law
explanation: Rule 010101 & Ch 10: To the State Civil Service Commission and competent Courts of Law as provided by the Constitution.
source: Lagos State Public Service Rules, Rule 010101 and Chapter 10

question: A petitioner asks a prominent politician to press his case. What is the position?
options: It is permitted if the politician is the officer's own representative in the Legislature
It is prohibited; officers must not seek the influence of prominent persons
It is permitted provided the petition is also routed through the Permanent Secretary
It is permitted, but the officer must declare the politician's involvement in the petition
explanation: Rule 040528: Prohibited; officers must not seek the influence of prominent persons to press petitions.
source: Lagos State Public Service Rules, Rule 040528

question: The Ministry receives a petition signed with a false name. How is it treated?
options: It is investigated, and the identity of the real petitioner is traced for disciplinary action only
It is treated as valid, since the content of the petition matters and not the signature
It is returned to the Registry to be registered under the false name as the petitioner
Generally disregarded, since anonymous petitions are discountenanced
explanation: Rule 100204: Petitions with false or anonymous names are generally disregarded and discountenanced.
source: Lagos State Public Service Rules, Rule 100204

question: In a petition written on behalf of an illiterate person, whom must the jurat indicate?
options: The writer/interpreter of the petition
The Permanent Secretary who received the petition
The Commissioner for Oaths who swore the illiterate person
The legal practitioner who advised the illiterate person
explanation: Rule 100205: The jurat must specifically indicate the writer/interpreter of the petition.
source: Lagos State Public Service Rules, Rule 100205

question: Which is the correct order of routing a petition?
options: Permanent Secretary, then immediate superior officer, then the final appellate authority
Immediate superior officer, then the final appellate authority, then the Permanent Secretary
Immediate superior officer, then the Permanent Secretary, then the final appellate authority
Final appellate authority, then Permanent Secretary, then immediate superior officer
explanation: Rule 100206: The correct routing order is immediate superior officer, Permanent Secretary, then final appellate authority.
source: Lagos State Public Service Rules, Rule 100206

question: A petitioner insults the Permanent Secretary in his petition. How is this viewed?
options: As a minor lapse of etiquette that does not affect the officer's disciplinary record
As an offence for which the petition is withdrawn and the officer warned verbally
As a matter that is handled solely within the petition without any other action
As misconduct that can attract separate disciplinary action
explanation: Chapter 10: Insulting a superior officer in a petition is viewed as misconduct that can attract disciplinary action.
source: Lagos State Public Service Rules, Chapter 10, General Standard

question: An officer who has been dismissed lodges a petition. From what date does the dismissal take effect?
options: The date the petition is decided
The date on which he is notified
The date of the next annual appraisal
Six months after notification
explanation: Rule 040509: Dismissal takes effect from the date on which the officer is notified.
source: Lagos State Public Service Rules, Rule 040509

question: Which of these is a prohibited way of airing a grievance?
options: Writing to the Permanent Secretary through proper channels and keeping copies
Counselling sessions with a supervisor before a petition is lodged
Giving press interviews or publishing it without express government permission
A formal appeal against a disciplinary decision to the appropriate appellate body
explanation: Rule 040522: Giving press interviews or publishing grievances without express permission is prohibited.
source: Lagos State Public Service Rules, Rule 040522

question: Under which law is an officer bound regarding classified information and state secrets?
options: The Official Secrets Act (Cap. 335)
The National Security Agencies Act (Cap. N74)
The Public Complaints Commission Act (Cap. P37)
The Freedom of Information Act (Cap. F43)
explanation: Rule 040517: Officers are bound by the Official Secrets Act (Cap. 335).
source: Lagos State Public Service Rules, Rule 040517

question: What is the effect of a malicious and false petition?
options: It is minor misconduct punishable by a query and a written warning
It is serious misconduct punishable by dismissal
It is serious misconduct punishable by interdiction for one year without pay
It is general inefficiency punishable by a deferment of increment
explanation: Rule 040502: Submitting malicious and false petitions constitutes serious misconduct punishable by dismissal.
source: Lagos State Public Service Rules, Rule 040502(xxvii)

question: Before an officer petitions the Head of Government directly, what must he have done?
options: Obtained the consent of his Permanent Secretary and a letter of support from his trade union
Waited for a period of twelve months after the decision before petitioning
Obtained a ruling from the Civil Service Commission refusing the grievance in writing
Exhausted internal departmental channels and routed the petition properly
explanation: Rule 100104: The officer must have exhausted internal departmental channels and routed properly.
source: Lagos State Public Service Rules, Rule 100104

question: A petition is filed late. What must the petitioner do?
options: Explain the delay
Pay a fine
Say nothing about it
Withdraw the petition
explanation: Rule 100208: The petitioner must explain the delay to avoid disqualification.
source: Lagos State Public Service Rules, Rule 100208

question: Which of the following must appear at the end of a formal petition?
options: The petitioner's signature, rank, ministry and date, together with the Permanent Secretary's remarks
The petitioner's and a witness's signatures, service number, and the prayer
The petitioner's signature, rank, ministry, date and the prayer/desired remedy
The petitioner's signature, rank, ministry and date, with a list of the attached exhibits
explanation: Rule 100209: The petitioner's signature, rank, ministry, date and prayer/desired remedy must appear at the end.
source: Lagos State Public Service Rules, Rule 100209

question: Can an officer be victimized for lodging a legitimate, properly channeled petition?
options: Yes, if the petition is later dismissed, he may be transferred as a measure of discipline
Yes, but only where the petition criticised a superior officer in the same department
Yes, because a petition is a personal matter and carries no protection under the Rules
No, victimization is prohibited and amounts to administrative misconduct
explanation: Chapter 10: Victimization is prohibited and constitutes administrative misconduct.
source: Lagos State Public Service Rules, Chapter 10, General Principles

question: Before escalating a grievance to a formal petition, what does the Service encourage?
options: Immediate referral of the grievance to the Civil Service Commission for a hearing
Counselling, mentoring, coaching and dialogue with supervisors
Informal complaint to the officer's trade union before approaching superiors
Transfer of the aggrieved officer to another unit pending a formal investigation
explanation: Rule 040302 & Ch 10: Counselling, mentoring, coaching and dialogue with supervisors are encouraged.
source: Lagos State Public Service Rules, Rule 040302 and Chapter 10

question: Through which body does an appeal from a parastatal organization first pass?
options: The Head of Service and the Civil Service Commission, in that order
The Governing Board/Council alone, with no input from the supervisory Ministry
The Parastatal Governing Board/Council and supervisory Ministry
The supervisory Ministry's Permanent Secretary and the Head of Government
explanation: Rule 180601: The Parastatal Governing Board/Council and supervisory Ministry.
source: Lagos State Public Service Rules, Rule 180601

question: Which office coordinates administrative reviews and advisory processing on personnel appeals?
options: The Public Service Office
The State Board of Internal Revenue
A private firm
The officer's cooperative society
explanation: Chapters 6 & 10: The Public Service Office coordinates administrative reviews and advisory processing.
source: Lagos State Public Service Rules, Chapters 6 and 10

question: What must accompany a petition containing allegations about financial records?
options: A sworn affidavit from the petitioner and an unsigned statement from a colleague
Detailed audit reports, vouchers and documentary evidence
A letter of support from the officer's trade union and the petitioner's bank statements
A written undertaking to bear the cost of any audit that may be required
explanation: Rule 100202: Detailed audit reports, vouchers and documentary evidence must accompany allegations involving finances.
source: Lagos State Public Service Rules, Rule 100202

question: Who handles appeals relating to officers on Grade Level 07 and above?
options: The Head of Service or the Permanent Secretary of the officer's ministry
The Personnel Management Board of the officer's ministry
The Director of Personnel Management through the Office of Establishments
The State Civil Service Commission or the relevant Extra-Ministerial Body
explanation: Chapter 10 & 2: The State Civil Service Commission or relevant Extra-Ministerial Body handles appeals for GL 07 and above.
source: Lagos State Public Service Rules, Chapter 10 and Chapter 2, Section 6

question: What is the consequence of a civil servant failing without reasonable excuse to appear before a Commission when requested?

Assure that the contractor will complete the works within the stated period

explanation: Guarantees that the bidder will not withdraw its bid or will sign the contract if awarded.

Ensure that the contractor pays all taxes due to the State Government
Assure that the contractor will perform the contract satisfactorily
explanation: Assures that the contractor will perform the contract satisfactorily.

Suspending a contractor temporarily from a contract pending the outcome of an audit

Cancelling a procurement process because of lack of funds

The highest quality available irrespective of cost or timeliness

Approving the award and signing the contract on behalf of the procuring entity
Advertising the procurement opportunity and selling the bidding documents
Receiving bids and issuing receipts to bidders at the bid submission

source: Lagos State Civil Service Practice Questions, Lagos State Public Procurement Law (2021)
